title: Two Sum
prompt: Input: an integer array nums and an integer target. Output: indices of the two numbers that add up to target. Constraints: exactly one solution exists; aim for O(n) time.

title: Valid Parentheses
prompt: Input: a string of the characters ()[]{}. Output: true if every bracket is closed by the same type in the correct order. Constraints: length up to 10^4.

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
prompt: Input: heads of two sorted linked lists. Output: head of one merged sorted list built by splicing nodes. Constraints: up to 50 nodes each.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
prompt: Input: an array prices where prices[i] is the price on day i. Output: the maximum profit from one buy then one later sell (0 if none). Constraints: up to 10^5 days; O(n).

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
prompt: Input: a string s. Output: the length of the longest substring with no repeated characters. Constraints: length up to 5*10^4; O(n) sliding window expected.

title: 3Sum
prompt: Input: an integer array nums. Output: all unique triplets that sum to zero. Constraints: no duplicate triplets; length up to 3000.

title: Number of Islands
prompt: Input: an m x n grid of '1' (land) and '0' (water). Output: the number of islands (4-directionally connected land). Constraints: m, n up to 300.

title: Course Schedule
prompt: Input: numCourses and a list of prerequisite pairs. Output: true if all courses can be finished (no cycle). Constraints: up to 2000 courses, 5000 pairs.

title: Top K Frequent Elements
prompt: Input: an integer array nums and k. Output: the k most frequent elements in any order. Constraints: better than O(n log n).

title: Product of Array Except Self
prompt: Input: an integer array nums. Output: an array where output[i] is the product of all elements except nums[i]. Constraints: O(n) time, no division.

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
prompt: Input: an array of k sorted linked lists. Output: one merged sorted list. Constraints: k up to 10^4, total nodes up to 10^4; O(N log k).

title: Trapping Rain Water
prompt: Input: n non-negative integers representing an elevation map. Output: how much water it traps after raining. Constraints: n up to 2*10^4; O(n) time.

title: Word Ladder
prompt: Input: beginWord, endWord and a word list. Output: the number of words in the shortest transformation sequence changing one letter at a time (0 if none). Constraints: list up to 5000 words.

title: Serialize and Deserialize Binary Tree
prompt: Input: the root of a binary tree. Output: a string encoding and a decoder that rebuilds the identical tree. Constraints: up to 10^4 nodes.

title: Minimum Window Substring
prompt: Input: strings s and t. Output: the smallest substring of s containing every character of t (with multiplicity), or empty. Constraints: lengths up to 10^5; O(m+n).

title: Design Pastebin (or a URL shortener)
prompt: Design a service where users paste text and get a short shareable link that expires. Cover API, storage, ID generation, read-heavy scaling, and expiry.

title: Scale a web app to millions of users
prompt: Design the architecture that takes a web app from a single server to millions of users: load balancing, caching, database replication and sharding, and async work.

title: Design the Twitter timeline and search
prompt: Design home and user timelines plus tweet search for hundreds of millions of users. Cover fan-out on write vs. read, caching, and search indexing.

title: Design a web crawler
prompt: Design a crawler that fetches a billion pages a month, avoids duplicates, respects robots rules, and feeds a search index. Cover the URL frontier, politeness, and dedupe.

title: Design Mint.com (personal finance aggregation)
prompt: Design a service that connects to users' bank accounts, imports transactions daily, categorizes them, and alerts on budgets. Cover ingestion, idempotency, and analytics.

title: Design Amazon's sales rank by category
prompt: Design a system that computes hourly best-seller rankings per category from a stream of orders. Cover batch vs. streaming aggregation and serving.

title: Design a chat service (WhatsApp)
prompt: Design one-to-one and group messaging with delivery receipts, offline delivery, and presence for a billion users. Cover connections, ordering, and storage.

title: Design a distributed rate limiter
prompt: Design a rate limiter used by an API gateway across many nodes, supporting per-user and per-endpoint limits. Cover algorithms, shared state, and failure modes.

title: Design a notification system
prompt: Design a service that sends push, email, and SMS notifications with user preferences, retries, deduplication, and rate limits.

title: Design a ride-hailing service (Uber)
prompt: Design rider-driver matching, live location tracking, pricing, and trip state for a global ride-hailing service. Cover geo-indexing and consistency.

title: Design a video streaming service (Netflix)
prompt: Design upload, transcoding, CDN distribution, and adaptive playback for a global video service. Cover storage tiers, cost, and recommendations at a high level.

title: Design real-time collaborative editing (Google Docs)
prompt: Design a document editor where many users edit concurrently with low latency and no lost edits. Cover OT vs. CRDTs, presence, offline edits, and storage.

title: Design a distributed tracing system
prompt: Design a system that collects spans from thousands of microservices, samples intelligently, and lets engineers query a trace end to end within seconds.

title: Design a payments ledger
prompt: Design a double-entry ledger for a payments company that records every money movement exactly once, supports reconciliation with banks, and stays auditable.

title: Design Tic-Tac-Toe
prompt: Design classes for an N x N tic-tac-toe game with two players, move validation, and O(1) win detection.

title: Design a vending machine
prompt: Design the classes and state machine for a vending machine that accepts coins and notes, dispenses items, returns change, and handles sold-out items.

title: Design a logging framework
prompt: Design a logger with levels, multiple sinks (console, file), formatting, and thread-safe writes. Show how new sinks are added without changing callers.

title: Design Snake and Ladder
prompt: Design classes for a multiplayer snake-and-ladder game with a configurable board, dice, and turn handling.

title: Design a parking lot
prompt: Design classes for a multi-level parking lot with different spot sizes, ticketing, fee calculation, and availability display.

title: Design an elevator system
prompt: Design classes for a building with several elevators: request handling, direction logic, and a pluggable dispatch strategy.

title: Design an LRU cache class
prompt: Design a generic LRU cache class with get and put in O(1), capacity eviction, and a clear interface for swapping eviction policies.

title: Design a library management system
prompt: Design classes for members, books, copies, loans, reservations, and fines, with clear responsibilities and extension points.

title: Design Splitwise (expense sharing)
prompt: Design classes to add shared expenses with equal, exact, and percentage splits, track balances, and simplify debts between users.

title: Design a movie ticket booking system
prompt: Design classes for theaters, shows, seats, and bookings, including temporary seat holds and preventing double booking under concurrency.

title: Design a concurrent in-memory key-value store with TTL
prompt: Design a thread-safe key-value store with per-key TTL, lazy and active expiry, snapshots, and a pluggable eviction policy. Discuss locking granularity.

title: Design a stock exchange order-matching engine
prompt: Design the classes for an order book that matches limit and market orders by price-time priority, supports cancels, and emits trade events.

title: Disagreement with a teammate
prompt: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate on a technical approach. How did you resolve it, and what was the outcome?

title: Owning a production issue
prompt: Describe a production incident you owned end to end. What did you do in the moment and what did you change afterward?

title: A project that failed
prompt: Tell me about a project that missed its goal or deadline. What was your part in it and what did you learn?

title: Working with unclear requirements
prompt: Describe a time you started work with vague or changing requirements. How did you create clarity and decide what to build first?

title: Influencing without authority
prompt: Tell me about a time you convinced another team to change their plans without having authority over them.

title: Pushing back on a manager
prompt: Describe a time you disagreed with your manager's decision. How did you raise it and what happened?

title: Paying down tech debt
prompt: Tell me about a time you identified technical debt that was slowing the team and got the work prioritized and done.

title: Growing another engineer
prompt: Describe how you mentored an engineer through a hard problem. How did you balance helping with letting them own it?

title: A technical decision you got wrong
prompt: Tell me about a significant technical decision you made that turned out wrong. How did you find out, and how did you correct course?

title: Leading a cross-team technical change
prompt: Describe a technical initiative you led across several teams. How did you set direction, get buy-in, and measure success?

title: Changing a leadership decision
prompt: Tell me about a time you changed the mind of senior leadership on a strategic technical direction. What data and arguments did you use?

title: Defining strategy in a new problem space
prompt: Describe a time you were asked to own a problem space with no roadmap. How did you decide the strategy and what did you deliberately not do?

title: Resolving a cross-team conflict
prompt: Tell me about a sustained conflict between two teams over priorities or ownership. What role did you play in resolving it?
